title: Maximal isometric trunk flexion moment at L5-S1 (semi-seated dynamometer), males
condition: isometric maximal flexion exertion against a harness, semi-seated, feet/knees/pelvis stabilised

quantity.name: maximal resistant moment at L5-S1
quantity.definition: mean±SD of maximal flexion moment at L5-S1 over 12 subjects (magnitude); plus measured moments of the 4 modelled subjects (Table 1). Coupled moments not reported.

source.authors: El Ouaaid Z, Shirazi-Adl A, Plamondon A, Lariviere C
source.sample: healthy male university students, no back pain history, in vivo

protocol.summary: Trunk dynamometer with three triaxial AMTI MC6-6-1000 force platforms on a steel frame stabilising feet, knees and pelvis (similar to Lariviere 2009); semi-seated position; 10-s maximal pushes against a harness (3 trials extension, 2 flexion, 2 per side lateral and axial); moments at L5-S1 recorded at 128 Hz. Harness-trunk contact: anterior-directed force at T8 in extension; force normal to sternum at T6 in flexion.
how_to_simulate: Semi-seated posture, pelvis fixed; trunk flexed forward; prescribed rotations from upright standing: +15 deg (extension) at S1 and -11 deg at T12, T12-S1 difference partitioned 8/14/16/22/25/15% from T12-L1 to L5-S1.
Apply the harness reaction (T6, normal to sternum) with magnitude producing the measured L5-S1 moment; add upper-body gravity scaled to body weight.
Compare model maximal moment (or required max muscle stress / saturation) with data; use Table 1 individual moments for subject-specific runs.

subject_model.source: Methods 2.1 (mean of 12); per-subject body weights for 4 modelled subjects in Table 1 (68, 76, 68.3, 72.8 kg)

protocol.notes: Flexion < extension (p=0.0005). Same IRSST lab/dynamometer as Ghezelbash 2018 but a different cohort (12 males). Paper's model also assumed IAP up to 25 kPa (flexion) / 10 kPa (extension).

extraction.check_notes: Text values checked against Fig 3 moment bars (digitised flexion ~151, extension ~242 Nm on right axis) and Table 1 re-read from rendered page.
